fullPassage: Emphasizing speed over frequency can make sense in contexts where everyone is expected to plan around the timetable, including peak-only commute services and very long trips with low demand. In all other contexts, though, it seems to be a common motorist's error. Roads are there all the time, so their speed is the most important fact that distinguishes them. But transit is only there if it's coming soon. If you have a car, you can use a road whenever you want and experience its speed. But transit has to exist when you need it (span), and it needs to be coming soon (frequency). Otherwise, waiting time will wipe out any time savings from a faster service. Unless you're comfortable planning your life around a particular scheduled trip, speed is worthless without frequency, so a transit map that screams about speed and whispers about frequency may simply be planting confusion.

But transit is only there if it's coming soon. If you have a car, you can use a road whenever you want and experience its ______. But transit has to exist when you need it (span), and it needs to be coming soon (frequency). Otherwise, waiting time will wipe out any time savings from a faster service. Unless you're comfortable planning your life around a particular scheduled trip, ______ is worthless without frequency, so a transit map that screams about velocity and whispers about frequency may simply be planting confusion.
questions.stem: 본문에 따르면 도로(Roads)의 가장 중요한 특성은 무엇인지 영어 한 단어로 쓰시오.

det.korean: speed(속도). Roads are there all the time, so their speed is the most important fact.
det.analysis: speed: 도로는 항상 존재하므로 속도가 가장 중요한 요소
det.tip: their speed is the most important fact

questions.passage: Emphasizing speed over frequency can make sense in contexts where everyone is expected to plan around the timetable, including peak-only commute services and very long trips with low demand. In all other contexts, though, it seems to be a common motorist's error. Roads are there all the time, so their speed is the most important fact that distinguishes them. But transit is only there if it's coming soon. If you have a car, you can use a road whenever you want and experience its speed. But transit has to exist when you need it (span), and it needs to be coming soon (frequency). Otherwise, waiting time will wipe out any time savings from a faster service. Unless you're comfortable planning your life around a particular scheduled trip, speed is worthless without frequency, so a transit map that screams about speed and whispers about frequency may simply be planting ______.
questions.stem: 본문의 마지막 문장에서, 노선도가 결국 유발할 수 있다고 한 것은 무엇인지 영어 한 단어로 쓰시오.

det.korean: confusion(혼란). planting confusion = 혼란을 심다.
det.analysis: confusion: 속도만 강조하는 노선도가 혼란을 유발
det.tip: planting confusion = 혼란을 심다/유발하다
